mainTopic: Who must bring proof when a person who gave away all his property says he was a שכיב מרע (deathly ill) and the receivers say he was healthy, and whether this מחלוקת between רבי יעקב and רבי נתן lines up with the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about a girl who became a בוגרת during the day.
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about a man who gave away all his property and later says he was a שכיב מרע, while the receivers say he was healthy. רבי יעקב says the giver gets the property back unless the receivers prove he was healthy. רבי נתן says it depends on how the man is now. The גמרא asks whether רב and שמואל, who argue about a girl who became a בוגרת, simply follow these two תנאים. Each אמורא shows his view can fit both תנאים. Two ברייתות about a girl betrothed by her father and by herself also turn out to agree, depending on whether she denies her father's power. But שמואל's anger at רב יוסף shows that רב and שמואל really disagree, and the final הלכה follows רב. A new משנה then teaches when a man returning from overseas must prove the lineage of his wife and children. The גמרא adds that children need no proof only when they cling to the mother, and only when there is one wife. A statement of רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: Who can take the property from whom?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which side can take the property away from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who takes the property out of whose hands?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks who wins the property when the giver says he was deathly ill and the receivers say he was healthy. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the giver was a שכיב מרע, he can take his gift back now that he is better. If he was healthy, the gift stands. The question is about who has to bring proof and who can take the property without proof.

keyTerms.meaning: takes out, takes away (here: wins the property from the other side)
from the hand of, from the possession of
a person who is deathly ill; his gifts can be taken back if he gets better

phrases.english: Who takes out from the hand of whom?
phrases.notes: He means: who gets to take the property away from the other side?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that the גמרא is quoting to compare to the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side must bring proof: the giver who says he was a שכיב מרע, or the receivers who say he was healthy?

steps.title: רבי יעקב and רבי נתן disagree about who must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says the giver can take the property back without proof, and they cannot take it from him without proof. רבי נתן says it depends on whether he is healthy or sick right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can take the property from them without proof, and they cannot take it from him without proof. These are the words of רבי יעקב. רבי נתן says: if he is healthy now, he must bring proof that he was deathly ill. If he is deathly ill now, they must bring proof that he was healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives two answers. רבי יעקב says the property goes to the giver, its original owner, unless the receivers prove he was healthy, while רבי נתן decides by the man's condition right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יעקב, the question of his health back then stays a doubt, so the property stays with its original owner, the giver. For רבי נתן, his current condition counts. If he is healthy now, we assume he was healthy then too, so he needs proof. If he is sick now, we assume he was sick then too, so they need proof.

keyTerms.meaning: proof
healthy
the job of bringing proof is on him

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' in רבי יעקב's opinion is always the giver, and 'they' are the receivers. רבי יעקב means the property stays with the giver unless they bring proof.

phrases.english: He takes it out of their hands without proof,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the giver who says he was sick; 'they' are the people who received the gift.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן אֵין מוֹצִיאִים מִיָּדוֹ בְּלֹא רְאָיָה,
phrases.english: and they cannot take it out of his hands without proof,
these are the words of Rabbi Yaakov.
Rabbi Natan says:
If he is healthy now,

phrases.aramaic: עָלָיו לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁהָיָה שְׁכִיב מְרַע,
phrases.english: it is on him to bring proof that he was deathly ill,
and if he is deathly ill now,
it is on them to bring proof that he was healthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יעקב: the property stays with the giver unless the receivers bring proof. רבי נתן: go by his condition now; whoever claims a change from it must bring proof.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב leaves the property with its owner. רבי נתן goes by the person's condition right now.

steps.title: Does רב follow רבי נתן and שמואל follow רבי יעקב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל is the same as the מחלוקת of רבי נתן and רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב follows רבי נתן, and שמואל follows רבי יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל are simply repeating the older מחלוקת of the תנאים. This sets up the next two steps, where each אמורא pushes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב goes by how the girl is now, a בוגרת, just as רבי נתן goes by how the man is now. שמואל leaves the question as a doubt and worries about both betrothals, just as רבי יעקב leaves the question of the man's health as a doubt. If this match were true, each אמורא would be bound to one side of the תנאים' מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (the גמרא offers a suggestion to test)
like, in agreement with

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav spoke like Rabbi Natan,
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב's ruling about the girl who became a בוגרת: we go by how she is now.

phrases.english: and Shmuel spoke like Rabbi Yaakov?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 2 to try to explain the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל the same as the מחלוקת of רבי נתן and רבי יעקב?

steps.title: רב: my view works even according to רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב says רבי יעקב keeps things in their old state only for money, not for a body that naturally changes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could tell you: I said my ruling even according to רבי יעקב. רבי יעקב said his rule only there, where we can say 'leave the money in its old state.' But here, can we say 'leave the body in its old state'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב rejects the suggestion and shows that רבי יעקב could agree with him. Money stays put, but a growing girl's body does not stay the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב's reason is חזקת ממון: property stays with the person who already owns it. A girl's body is different, because she naturally grows up, so there is no reason to assume she stayed a נערה. That means even רבי יעקב would agree we go by how she is now.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
he only said his rule up to here (limits an opinion to its own case)
leave the money in its earlier state (with its owner)
body
there / here

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
I said my ruling even according to Rabbi Yaakov.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov only said his rule there,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הַעֲמֵד מָמוֹן עַל חֶזְקָתוֹ,
phrases.english: where one can say: leave the money in its earlier state,
but here, can we say:
leave the body in its earlier state?!
phrases.notes: A girl's body grows up on its own, so you can't assume it stayed the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 3 for רב's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב must follow רבי נתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יעקב's reason (חזקת ממון) applies to property, not to a body that naturally changes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between a presumption about money staying put and a presumption about a body, which naturally changes over time.

steps.title: שמואל: my view works even according to רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רבי נתן put the proof on the giver only because everyone is presumed healthy, and in the girl's case there is no such presumption that she was a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: I said my ruling even according to רבי נתן. רבי נתן said his rule only there, because everyone is presumed healthy, so whoever takes himself out of that presumption must bring proof. But here, is she taking herself out of a presumption that was there before her?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל rejects the suggestion for his side, showing that רבי נתן could agree with him. The healthy-man case has a clear presumption of health, but the girl's case has nothing like it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן's real reason is not just 'go by now'; it is that all people are בחזקת בריאים, presumed healthy, so the man claiming sickness must prove it. In the girl's case, there was no earlier presumption that she was a בוגרת in the morning, so her being a בוגרת now proves nothing about then. So שמואל can still worry about both betrothals.

keyTerms.meaning: all people, everyone
presumed to be healthy
takes himself out of a presumption
to bring proof

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים fit with both תנאים. רבי יעקב's rule is about money staying with its owner, not about a body that changes. רבי נתן's rule is about everyone being presumed healthy, and there is no matching presumption that the girl was a בוגרת.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
I said my ruling even according to Rabbi Natan.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan only said his rule there,
because everyone stands in the presumption of being healthy,
so whoever takes himself out of that presumption,
it is on him to bring proof,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא מִי קָא מַפְּקָא נַפְשַׁהּ
phrases.english: but here, is she taking herself out
of a presumption that was there before?
phrases.notes: There was never a presumption that she was already a בוגרת in the morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches step 4 by rejecting the suggestion of step 3 for שמואל's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that שמואל must follow רבי יעקב (and cannot fit רבי נתן).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי נתן's rule rests on the general presumption of health, and the girl's case has no such presumption.

steps.title: Are רב and שמואל just repeating an argument of two ברייתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל match two ברייתות that rule differently about a girl married off by both her father and herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like an argument between תנאים. A father married off his daughter while on the road, and she married herself off in the city, and now she is a בוגרת. One ברייתא says: she is a בוגרת in front of us. Another ברייתא says: we worry about both marriages. Isn't one like רב and one like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות about the same case that seem to rule differently. It suggests that one matches רב and the other matches שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא looks at how she is now, a בוגרת, so the father had no power and only her own marriage counts. That fits רב. The second ברייתא worries that both marriages may have worked, because we don't know when she grew up. That fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this matches an argument between these תנאים
A girl who is fully grown; her father can no longer marry her off
In front of us; we judge by how she is now
We are concerned; we treat it as a doubt
Is it not so that...? It introduces a suggested reading

phrases.english: Let us say it is like these Tanna'im:
Her father betrothed her on the road,
phrases.notes: The father was away traveling when he did this, so nobody knows if she was already grown at that moment.

phrases.english: and she betrothed herself in the city,
and she is now a grown woman;

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא חֲדָא: הֲרֵי הִיא בּוֹגֶרֶת לְפָנֵינוּ,
phrases.english: one baraisa taught: she is a grown woman before us,
and the other baraisa taught:
we are concerned for the betrothal of both of them.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: חַד כְּרַב וְחַד כִּשְׁמוּאֵל?
phrases.english: Is it not that one is like Rav and one is like Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attempt to link רב and שמואל to רבי יעקב and רבי נתן was pushed off, the גמרא tries a new pair of ברייתות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רב and שמואל argument already found as an argument between ברייתות?

steps.title: Both ברייתות can follow שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both ברייתות agree with שמואל. They just talk about different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, both follow שמואל. One talks about when she denies his claim, and one talks about when she does not deny it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתות argue. It says both can follow שמואל, because each one is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she claims she was already a בוגרת when her father acted, we believe her, and only her own marriage counts. If she makes no such claim, it is a real doubt, so we worry about both marriages. So there is no argument between the ברייתות at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one; both
She contradicts him; she says she was already grown when he acted
Here... here...; each source is about a different case

phrases.english: No, both this and that are like Shmuel —
here, where she contradicts him,
phrases.notes: She says she was already grown before her father betrothed her, so he had no power to do it.

phrases.english: here, where she does not contradict him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 6 by splitting the ברייתות into two different cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the two ברייתות match רב and שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות are not arguing. One is about when she denies her father's power, and the other is about when she doesn't.

steps.title: Maybe רב and שמואל don't argue either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that, just like the ברייתות, רב and שמואל might each be talking about a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say: just as the ברייתות don't argue, the אמוראים also don't argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the answer from step 7 one step further. It sets up the idea that רב and שמואל may not disagree at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case can be split into 'she denies' and 'she doesn't deny', then maybe רב is talking about when she denies, and שמואל about when she doesn't. Then there would be no real argument between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means the ברייתות
The אמוראים; here, רב and שמואל
They don't disagree

phrases.english: And let us say: since the baraisos do not disagree,
the Amora'im also do not disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the split from step 7 to suggest that רב and שמואל might also agree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could רב and שמואל also be talking about two different cases, so that they don't really disagree?

steps.title: שמואל's anger shows they really disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the idea from step 8. שמואל got upset when רב יוסף ruled like רב, so it seems they really disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? רב יוסף son of רב מנשיא of Davil ruled like רב, and שמואל got upset. He said: 'Everyone gets wisdom in a small measure, and this scholar gets it in a big measure?' If they don't disagree, why was he upset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 8 with a real story. A judge ruled like רב, and שמואל was angry about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's sarcastic line means: 'Does this man think he is so much wiser than everyone else that he can rule against me?' Being angry only makes sense if רב's ruling went against שמואל's view. That suggests רב and שמואל truly disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you think so? It opens a challenge
He did an action; he gave a real ruling
He was upset or offended
A קב, a measuring container
It enters your mind; if you were to think

phrases.english: And can you think so?

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא מִדְּוִויל
phrases.english: But Rav Yosef, son of Rav Menashya of Davil,
did an action according to Rav,
and Shmuel was upset and said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כָּיְילִי לֵיהּ בְּקַבָּא זוּטָא
phrases.english: Everyone has it measured out to him in a small kav,
phrases.notes: He is being sarcastic. 'It' means wisdom.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי מִדְּרַבָּנַן כָּיְילִי לֵיהּ בְּקַבָּא רַבָּה?
phrases.english: and this one of the Sages has it measured out in a big kav?
And if it enters your mind that they don't disagree,
why was he upset?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? הָא רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא מִדְּוִויל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 8's idea that רב and שמואל don't disagree.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from step 8 that רב and שמואל are each talking about a different case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל was angry at a ruling that followed רב. That only makes sense if רב's view goes against שמואל's view.

steps.title: Maybe רב יוסף's case was one where she denied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב יוסף's real case may have been one where the girl denied her father's power.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when he gave his ruling, it was a case where she contradicted him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to read the story about רב יוסף. Maybe his case was one where the girl said she was already grown when her father acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a case where she denies, even שמואל agrees that the father's marriage doesn't count. So רב יוסף's ruling, by itself, doesn't prove that רב and שמואל argue. The line asks us to look again at what the story about שמואל's anger really shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; it offers another possible reading

steps.confusionAlert: This short line can be read in two ways. Some read it as answering step 9: the ruling was in a case of מכחשתו, and שמואל was upset only because he thought she was not denying. Others read it the opposite way: in such a case שמואל would have had no reason to be upset, so רב and שמואל must really argue.
steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות can both follow שמואל: if she denies her father's power, only her marriage counts; if she doesn't, we worry about both. Whether רב and שמואל themselves truly argue depends on how we read the story of שמואל's anger at רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Perhaps when he did the action,
it was where she contradicted him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 9's proof from שמואל's anger by suggesting what the real case was.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the story may have been a case of מכחשתו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's anger proves that רב and שמואל really argue.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף's case may have been one where she denied, where even שמואל agrees. So the story alone does not settle whether they argue.

steps.title: Two later rulings on the רב–שמואל dispute
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא tells רב אשי that אמימר ruled like שמואל, while רב אשי himself rules like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said to רב אשי: אמימר said the הלכה follows שמואל. But רב אשי said the הלכה follows רב.
steps.whatsHappening: Later teachers now try to decide the practical הלכה in the רב–שמואל argument. Two of them give opposite rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 suggested that רב and שמואל might not really argue, but step 9 argued from שמואל's anger that they do. Step 10's short reply is read in different ways. Either way, later teachers now rule between רב and שמואל: אמימר sides with שמואל, and רב אשי sides with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה, meaning the ruling we actually follow
Like the opinion of (someone)
This is what (he) said; used when reporting someone else's ruling

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra said to Rav Ashi:
This is what Ameimar said:
The halacha is like Shmuel.
And Rav Ashi said:
The halacha is like Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר אַמֵּימָר הִילְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over whether רב and שמואל really disagree, the גמרא moves to deciding the halacha between them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר rules like שמואל; רב אשי rules like רב.

steps.title: Final ruling follows רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא decides that the הלכה follows רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its own final decision. It sides with רב (and with רב אשי) against אמימר's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This one short line ends the whole רב–שמואל discussion. Even though שמואל seemed upset when רב יוסף ruled like רב in step 9, the final practical ruling still follows רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And the (final) הלכה is; the גמרא's own closing decision

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of a girl married off by both her father and herself, the final הלכה follows רב.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two lines with the same words, "הילכתא כוותיה דרב". The first is רב אשי's personal opinion. The second, which starts with "ו־", is the גמרא's final decision.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rav.
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own final voice, not רב אשי speaking again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opposite rulings in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב in the dispute with שמואל.

steps.title: משנה: Man returns with the wife he left with
steps.stepSummary: If a man left with his wife and returns saying "this is her and these are her children," he needs no proof at all. If he says "she died, these are her children," he must prove the children are hers, but not her lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man went overseas with his wife and came back with his wife and children, and said: "This is the woman who went with me, and these are her children." He does not need to bring proof about the woman or about the children. If he says "she died, and these are her children," he must bring proof about the children, but not about the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses when a man coming back from overseas must prove the family background (יוחסין) of his wife and children. This first part covers a wife who was already his before he left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's lineage was already known when he married her before the trip, so she needs no proof. If she is here with the children, we can see they belong to her. If she died, nothing shows that these children are really hers, so he must prove it.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseas; a faraway land
Proof, here meaning evidence about family lineage
Here she is; this is her
Short for מתניתין, the משנה

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁיָּצָא הוּא וְאִשְׁתּוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who went overseas, he and his wife,
and came back, he and his wife and his children, and said:
"The woman who went overseas with me,
here she is, and these are her children":
he does not need to bring proof,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל הָאִשָּׁה, וְלֹא עַל הַבָּנִים.
phrases.english: not about the woman and not about the children.
phrases.notes: "About the woman" means about her family background, that she has proper lineage.

phrases.english: "She died, and these are her children":
he brings proof about the children,
phrases.notes: He has to prove these children were really born to that wife.

phrases.english: but he does not bring proof about the woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא הוּא וְאִשְׁתּוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It is not connected to the רב–שמואל discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If his wife was known before the trip, her lineage needs no proof. The children need proof only if she is no longer present.

steps.title: משנה: Man says he married overseas
steps.stepSummary: If he married her overseas and she is present, he must prove her lineage but not the children. If she died, he must prove both.
steps.simpleTranslation: "I married a woman overseas; here she is, and these are her children": he must bring proof about the woman, but not about the children. "She died, and these are her children": he must bring proof about the woman and about the children.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the opposite case: a wife he married while he was away. Nobody here knows her family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no one knows her background, her lineage must always be proven. Whether the children need proof again depends on whether she is here with them. If she died, both points are unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: I married
He is required to bring proof

steps.whatToRemember: There are two questions. Was her lineage known before the trip (if not, prove the woman)? And is she present with the children (if not, prove the children)?

phrases.english: "I married a woman overseas,
here she is, and these are her children":
he brings proof about the woman

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הַבָּנִים.
phrases.english: but does not need to bring proof about the children.
"She died, and these are her children":

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הָאִשָּׁה וְעַל הַבָּנִים.
phrases.english: he must bring proof about the woman and about the children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 13: a wife married overseas instead of one he left with.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife married overseas always needs proof of lineage. The children need proof only if she is not present.

steps.title: Children need no proof only when they cling to her
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says that every case in the משנה where the children need no proof is when they cling to the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: All of these cases are when the children cling to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a condition on the משנה. A man saying "these are her children" is only enough when the children actually cling to her like a mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה let him skip proof about the children when the woman is present. רבה בר רב הונא explains that her being present is not enough by itself. The children have to be attached to her, which shows she is their mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Clinging to her, attached to her the way children are to a mother
And all of them, meaning all the cases mentioned

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
And all of them are where they cling to her.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the cases in the משנה where he did not need proof about the children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא וְכוּלָּן בִּכְרוּכִים אַחֲרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's rule that the children need no proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The children need no proof only when they visibly cling to the woman as their mother.

steps.title: Married overseas: prove the wife and the adult children, not the young ones
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a man who married overseas must prove his wife's lineage and that of his adult children, but not that of his young children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If a man says "I married a woman overseas," he must bring proof about the woman's family, but not about the children. He must bring proof about the adult children, but not about the young children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up step 14 and adds a new detail. It splits the children into adults and young children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 already said a man who married overseas proves his wife's lineage but not the children's. The ברייתא adds that this only covers young children. Young children stay close to their mother, so everyone can see they are hers, which fits רבה בר רב הונא's rule in step 15. Adult children no longer cling to her, so their connection to her must be proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseas, a far-off land where nobody here knows the family.
Proof, such as witnesses showing the family is of proper lineage.
Adult children.
Young children (minors).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא contradicts itself. First it says "no proof about the children," then it says "proof about the adults." The second line explains the first: only the young children are exempt from proof.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If a man says, "I married a woman overseas"
he brings proof about the woman,
phrases.notes: He has to prove her family lineage is proper.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הַבָּנִים.
phrases.english: but he does not need to bring proof about the children.
And he brings proof about the adult children,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הַקְּטַנִּים.
phrases.english: but he does not need to bring proof about the young children.
phrases.notes: Young children cling to their mother, so it is plain to see they are hers.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִשָּׁה נָשָׂאתִי בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14 and adds a split between adult and young children, which fits the clinging rule of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who married overseas proves his wife's lineage and that of his adult children, but not that of his young children.

steps.title: The rule applies only to one wife; with two wives, everything needs proof
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule to a man with one wife. If he married two women overseas, he must prove the lineage of the women and of all the children, adult and young.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? With one wife. But if he married two women, he must bring proof about the woman and about the children, both the adults and the young ones. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ said:
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits its own rule: the young children are exempt only when there is one wife. At the end, the גמרא sets up a new statement by רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young children were exempt because their clinging to the mother shows whose they are. With two wives, a child clinging to one woman may really be the other wife's child being raised by her. So clinging no longer proves anything, and every child needs proof.

keyTerms.meaning: "In what case are these words said?" A phrase that limits an earlier rule to certain cases.
One wife.
Two wives.

steps.whatToRemember: Clinging to the mother proves whose child it is only when there is one possible mother. With two wives, the man must prove the lineage of every woman and every child.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the exemption rests on clear evidence, not on simply trusting the man. Once the evidence becomes unclear, the exemption is gone.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
With one woman,
but with two women

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הָאִשָּׁה וְעַל הַבָּנִים,
phrases.english: he brings proof about the woman and about the children,
phrases.notes: A child clinging to one wife might really be the other wife's child, being raised by this one.

phrases.english: both the adult ones and the young ones.
Reish Lakish said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's exemption from step 16 to a man with one wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two wives, the man must prove the lineage of the women and of all the children, both adult and young.
